title: Problem Overview
content: Erdős Problem #958: For n points in ℝ² with k = n-1 distinct distances and multiplicities {n-1,...,1}, must the points be equidistant on a line or circle? Answer: NO. Clemen-Dumitrescu-Liu (2025) found arc+center counterexamples. SOLVED.
mathContext: k = n-1 distances, multiplicities {n-1,...,1} ⟹ line/circle? FALSE.

title: Distance Framework
content: Point := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2). distanceSet(A) = set of distinct pairwise distances. multiplicity(A, d) = |{(p,q) : dist(p,q) = d}|. multiplicityMultiset(A) = multiset of all multiplicities. These definitions use Finset.product and Finset.image from Mathlib.
mathContext: distanceSet A = {‖p-q‖ : p,q ∈ A}. multiplicity A d = |{(p,q) ∈ A² : ‖p-q‖ = d}|.

title: Standard Configurations
content: isEquidistantLine(A, n): n points on a line with a common direction vector. isEquidistantCircle(A, n): n points on a circle of radius r > 0. isStandardConfig(A): line or circle configuration. These are the two classical configurations that satisfy the special multiplicity pattern.
mathContext: isStandardConfig A ≡ ∃ n, isEquidistantLine A n ∨ isEquidistantCircle A n.

title: Special Pattern and Conjecture
content: hasSpecialPattern(A): k = n-1 distinct distances and multiplicities form {1, 2, ..., n-1}. OriginalConjecture: hasSpecialPattern ↔ isStandardConfig for |A| ≥ 3. This conjecture turned out to be FALSE — there exist non-standard configurations with the special pattern.
mathContext: hasSpecialPattern A ≡ |distanceSet A| = n-1 ∧ multiplicityMultiset A = Multiset.range(n-1) + 1.

title: Arc Plus Center Configuration
content: isArcPlusCenter(A, n): n-1 equidistant points on a short arc of a unit circle plus the center. The arc must be short enough that all arc-to-arc distances are distinct and less than the diameter. The center has distance exactly 1 to every arc point, producing multiplicity n-1 for that distance.
mathContext: The key geometric insight: with n-1 arc points and 1 center, the center-to-arc distance d=1 has multiplicity n-1, and the arc-to-arc distances are all distinct with decreasing multiplicities.

title: Clemen-Dumitrescu-Liu Theorem and Disproof
content: clemen_dumitrescu_liu (axiom): For all n ≥ 4, there exists an arc+center configuration of n points that satisfies hasSpecialPattern but is NOT isStandardConfig. conjecture_disproved (axiom): ¬OriginalConjecture. Together these establish that the characterization fails for every n ≥ 4.
mathContext: ∀ n ≥ 4, ∃ A, isArcPlusCenter A n ∧ hasSpecialPattern A ∧ ¬isStandardConfig A.

title: Summary: SOLVED
content: erdos_958_summary: ¬OriginalConjecture ∧ (∀ n ≥ 4, ∃ counterexample). Proved from conjecture_disproved and clemen_dumitrescu_liu axioms using exact ⟨conjecture_disproved, clemen_dumitrescu_liu⟩. The characterization conjecture is FALSE — arc+center configurations provide a new infinite family of solutions.
mathContext: erdos_958_summary : ¬OriginalConjecture ∧ (∀ n ≥ 4, ∃ A, isArcPlusCenter A n ∧ hasSpecialPattern A ∧ ¬isStandardConfig A) := ⟨conjecture_disproved, clemen_dumitrescu_liu⟩.
